baseline.condition: Use only when the model leaves standard BBN expansion and thermodynamics intact; do not also use the D/H and helium likelihoods from which this prior was derived.

recommendation.do_not_use_if: The IVS model changes H(T), weak freeze-out, neutron abundance, or deuterium-burning time during BBN. In that case use observed abundance likelihood(s) and recompute BBN under IVS rather than applying an SBBN omega_b Gaussian.
recommendation.combination_rule: Alternative SBBN posteriors reuse the same abundance observations and different nuclear-rate assumptions; they are sensitivity models, not statistically independent likelihood factors.

observations.cutoff_search: Targeted arXiv/publisher search found no individual high-redshift absorber measurement later than the 2024 results listed below; PDG 2025 remains the latest broad official compilation identified.

latest_precision_measurements_found.locators: Abstract; §3.3/Fig. 6 for model systematic checks; Table 4/§5 for sample means

historical_homogeneous_measurement.locator: §4.3 and Eqs. 9-10; Eq. 11-12 old BBN mapping

uncertainty_assessment.pdg_prior_component_split: not separately reported; 0.00043 is combined SBBN error
uncertainty_assessment.reconstruction_method: Linearize D/H proportional to omega_b^-1.65 around omega_b≈0.0220 and D/H=2.508±0.030; subtract observation variance in quadrature from total 0.00022. Approximate, not a source-published split.
uncertainty_assessment.baseline_convention_difference: PDG §24.4 describes SBBN with N_nu=3; Poulin et al. use N_eff^SM=3.044. Treat results as related standard-physics implementations, not exactly identical calculations.

rate_network_comparison_at_planck_omega.locator: Table 2; LINX; uncertainty includes rate, neutron lifetime, and omega_b
